name: GRANSHAN — Base and Bloom
what: Two competitions focused exclusively on non-Latin scripts. Base judges typeface design itself; Bloom judges typefaces in real applications — posters, campaigns, packaging, motion, branding, editorial — across 9 media categories with 150+ jurors across 8 script groups.
why: Directly relevant if you build the bilingual specialism. Bloom accepts applied communication design, not just type design, so your existing Arabic–Latin work could enter.
prize: Not stated on the homepage — check the individual competition pages.
timing: Base: next edition 2027. Bloom: check the site.

name: Iron Viz
what: "The world's largest data visualization competition." An open qualifier round, then three finalists compete live on stage at Tableau Conference — 20 minutes each, same dataset.
why: Real prize money and a genuine platform. The qualifier is open to anyone in the Tableau community, and even the top ten get a gallery placement and a LinkedIn badge.
prize: 1st: $15,000 cash + $15,000 to a nonprofit of choice + trophy. 2nd and 3rd: $6,000 cash + $6,000 to a nonprofit each. Top 10: $200 Tableau Store gift card.
timing: Qualifier typically opens in the second half of the year and runs for one month. 2026 Championship: 5–7 May 2026, San Diego.

name: Malofiej International Infographics Awards
org: Society for News Design — Spanish chapter (SNDE), Universidad de Navarra
what: The long-running international infographics awards and summit, held in Pamplona, Spain.
why: The most prestigious award specifically for information graphics. Entering forces you to produce editorial-grade work rather than corporate-grade.
prize: Not stated on the navigation page.
timing: Annual, with the summit in Pamplona. Check the Awards section for the call for entries.

name: Morisawa Type Design Competition
what: Typeface design competition across five divisions: Japanese, Latin, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese and Hangeul. Plus a Fan Favorite decided by public vote.
why: A serious cash prize with no entry fee and no submission limit — one of the few competitions where the only cost is your time. The Latin division is open to you.
timing: Runs periodically — the most recent edition was 2024, with the ceremony in July 2025. Next edition not announced; watch the news section.
feeNote: "There is no limit to the number of submissions per entrant. No entry fee is charged."

name: Power BI DataViz World Championships
what: Three rounds of weekly visualisation challenges on supplied datasets, judged by a panel plus community voting, with one judge-selected wildcard. Culminates in a live finale at FabCon.
why: This is the one built exactly for what you already do. Global visibility inside the Microsoft ecosystem, and the rounds are short enough to enter around a job.
prize: Prizes are not stated in the announcement post — check the Fabric Community contest page.
timing: Rounds 1–3: 12 January – 2 February. Community voting: 19 January – 14 February. Finalists announced through February. Live finale: 16 March 2026.

name: Graphic Competitions
what: An aggregator of international creative calls — "illustration, photography, graphic design and multidisciplinary competitions, including deadlines, eligibility, fees and prizes." Free to browse, with a free weekly newsletter, an RSS feed and a calendar feed of deadlines.
why: This is the answer to "tell me when competitions are open". Its RSS feed is wired into the Latest stream, so every new call arrives automatically with its deadline — you do not have to remember to look.
prize: n/a — it lists other people's prizes.
timing: Continuous. Feed verified live on 9 September 2026.
feeNote: Free. Many listed competitions are marked "Free to enter".

name: Communication Arts — Design Competition
what: Juried competition covering posters, brochures, packaging, trademarks, corporate identity, annual reports, catalogs and signage.
why: Annual reports and corporate identity are explicit categories — one of the few major awards where the work you already do has a category of its own rather than being squeezed into 'branding'.
feeNote: Entry fees are not stated on the competitions page.

name: Communication Arts — Interactive Competition
what: Websites and microsites, environmental, mobile, social, tablet and handheld, and student work.
why: Where a well-built personal site or an interactive report can be entered as work in its own right.
feeNote: Entry fees are not stated on the competitions page.

name: Communication Arts — Typography Competition
what: Categories: collateral, packaging, media, motion, environmental, unpublished and experimental work, typeface designs, calligraphy and hand lettering.
why: The nearest deadline on this list and the lowest barrier — unpublished and experimental work is eligible, so you can enter something made specifically for it.
feeNote: Entry fees are not stated on the competitions page.

name: D&AD Awards
what: "The benchmark for creative bravery" — over 60 years old, awarding the D&AD Pencil across advertising and design. Categories include animation, cinematography, illustration, photography and sound.
why: The single most respected pencil in the industry. Even a shortlist changes how a CV is read, and D&AD is a registered charity that reinvests surplus into education.
timing: 2026 ceremony: 24 September 2026. New Blood ceremony: 30 June 2026. Entry windows open several months ahead — check the entry portal.
feeNote: Entry fees are not stated on the awards overview page; see the entry portal.

name: Information is Beautiful Awards
what: Celebrates "excellence and beauty in data visualizations and infographics" across nine categories and seven special awards, with longlists, shortlists and winners kept publicly browsable.
why: The one award where dashboard and information-design work is the main event rather than a side category. The kept archive also makes it a reference source, not just a competition.
timing: Annual. Entry involves a fee; the showcase is free to browse.
feeNote: Submission involves an entry fee, not specified on the homepage.

name: Red Dot Design Award
what: "An international design competition for product design, communication design and design concepts." The Brands & Communication Design track is the relevant one for corporate and identity work.
why: Widely recognised outside the design bubble, which makes it unusually useful when the audience for your CV is a corporate hiring panel rather than a creative director.
timing: Entry windows are not stated on the homepage — check the individual category pages.

name: Type Directors Club Competition
what: "The world's leading typography organization", running an annual global competition (currently TDC72) drawing entries from around 40 countries, with Best of Discipline and Judges' Choice winners, plus the new Type-High Awards medals.
why: The place to be recognised for typographic craft specifically — and the winning work travels as an international exhibition, which is unusually good exposure.
timing: Annual. Also runs three scholarships (Adé Hogue, Beatrice Warde, TDC) and the Type Drives Culture conference, expanding to Type Drives Commerce in 2026.

name: Dubai Lynx
what: Established 2007, "Home of MENA's creative marketing community" — a regional awards platform and Creativity Week for agencies, brand leaders, students and jurors.
why: The regional room worth being in. Attending is a networking decision more than a learning one, and it is close enough to attend without a flight budget.
timing: 2026: Creativity Week sessions 6–7 October, Awards Ceremony 8 October at Emirates Golf Club, Dubai.

name: Type Drives Culture / Type Drives Commerce
what: TDC's annual conference series, expanding to Type Drives Commerce in 2026.
why: A speaking opportunity worth aiming at within two years, once you have a bilingual typography case study worth presenting.
timing: Annual; check the site for the call for speakers.
